summary: Spades Mountain steel tower moved to Idaho's Long Mountain station in 1963-64, sold in 1998 and moved to private land east of Spokane; no tower is described at the site now.

facts.design: Aermotor MC-40 steel tower (1964 listing); 54 ft with a 12 x 12 wood cabin (1998 sale notice)
facts.status_note: Sold and moved in 1998 to private land east of Spokane, Washington; the Long Mountain site is listed as Tower Gone

staffing.status: Manned from July 1960 (announced: Larry Eaton and wife); Joyce Sprinkle began work in 1967, the latest staffing in these sources

events.note: Steel tower erected on Spades Mountain, Coeur d'Alene National Forest, Idaho; firetower.org gives it 54 ft
Newspaper item: a new forestry lookout station on Long Mountain nearing completion; the item does not mention the Spades tower
Announced to be manned from July 1 by Larry Eaton and his wife of Sandpoint
Moved from Spades Mountain to Long Mountain; 1963 per firetower.org and Idaho Fire Lookouts, 1964 per the NHLR and the Forest Lookouts page
Joyce Sprinkle of Tucson began work as fire lookout; latest staffing in these sources
Idaho Dept. of Lands offered the tower for sale, removal required by Sept 30, 1998; sold to Dave Kresek and moved to his property east of Spokane
Registered November 20, 1999 as US 329, WA 35 (Kresek Fire Tower)

corrections.why: The 1998 sale notice and Idaho Fire Lookouts both give 54 feet (16.5 m) for the tower on Long Mountain; 14.0 m matches only the 46-foot figure in the 1964 listing.

corrections.current: one undated event: 'The lookout was moved to Dave Kresek.'
corrections.proposed: 1963 move from Spades Mountain to Long Mountain (1964 in some sources); 1998 sale and move to Dave Kresek's property east of Spokane, WA
corrections.why: The single undated event leaves out the tower's arrival on Long Mountain and the 1998 date of the sale and move away.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: 1963 per firetower.org and Idaho Fire Lookouts; 1964 per the NHLR and the Forest Lookouts page. The story gives both years.
54 ft in the 1998 sale notice and Idaho Fire Lookouts (16.5 m used); 46 ft in the 1964 listing; the present Washington tower is 50 ft per the NHLR.

notes_for_editor: Two coordinate points conflict: the record uses the FFLA point 48.07989, -116.71415; Idaho Fire Lookouts gives 48.07657, -116.70825. Not resolved here. Staffing: a firelookout.com line that the tower 'had not been staffed for several years' was left out as ambiguous against the 1967 hire. A 1960 Weebly item calls the station the area's one surviving manned lookout and mentions a 'forest service lookout', which conflicts with the state agency; not used. The present-day tower is covered by us-wa-long-mountain-at-dave-kresek, which already exists. No source describes the Long Mountain site today.
